title: Missionary by nature (Ad Gentes 2)
tomorrow: who do people actually listen to: teachers or witnesses?

cards: The word mission can make a person wince: a knock at the door during dinner, a pamphlet pushed into a hand, a sales pitch with a halo on it.
So when a friend finally asks, honestly, why do you still go to church, it's easy to freeze, or to say "habit" just to avoid sounding like that. Is mission a job for a few professionals?
The council has a sentence about it that isn't a pitch at all. It's about where the Church comes from.

teach.b: Here's the sentence, from Ad Gentes, the decree on mission. The pilgrim Church, it says, is missionary by its very nature. Notice pilgrim: a Church still on the road.
Then the reason, and it isn't strategy. It's God's own life.

teach.h: FROM THE SENDING OF SON AND SPIRIT.
teach.b: The Church draws its origin, the decree says, from the mission of the Son and the mission of the Holy Spirit, according to the plan of God the Father.
Mission means a sending, and in this picture the first sending is God's.

teach.h: AS THE FATHER HATH SENT ME.
teach.b: In John's Gospel, the risen Jesus says it to his friends: "As the Father hath sent me, I also send you." The Church comes out of that sending, so it keeps going out.
Underneath, the decree says, the whole plan flows from the Father's love, like water from a spring that keeps pouring.
So mission isn't an activity the Church picks up on good days, and it isn't a job for a few specialists. It's what the whole Church is. And the council pairs going out with respect.
Its declaration on religious freedom, a few days back, says no one is ever to be forced.
Missionary by nature, then, never by force, and never as a pitch.

how: Catholics support missions through prayer and giving, and many parishes mark a yearly World Mission Sunday; the decree speaks of the whole Church as sent.

o: a church built far from any town or city
the whole Church is sent, because God first sends
a priest assigned to serve in another country

games.q: missionary by nature — tap the pairs.
p: a Church still on the road
the Father's love, like a spring

s: being missionary means pressuring people to join
the council's declaration on religious freedom says no one is to be forced.
the decree roots mission in the sending of the Son and the Spirit
according to the plan of the Father, flowing from his love.

it says the pilgrim Church is missionary by its very nature.

games.q: your parish asks every teen to "invite one friend" and post about it. a teammate feels pressured. what fits Ad Gentes and the no-coercion declaration together?
o: push harder: more posts mean more mission.
skip it: mission is for missionaries abroad.
invite freely, with no pressure on anyone.
games.why: the whole Church is sent, by its nature, and the council also says no one is ever to be forced. an invitation, freely given and freely refused, holds both.

practice: Bring to mind someone who might one day ask why you believe, or why you don't. See the moment, and notice the pull to dodge or to lecture. Plan one honest sentence about what it's actually like for you, and keep it ready.

wordCard.voice: Missionary by nature. Ad Gentes: the whole Church is sent, because it comes from God's own sending.

orig.note: Latin, 'to the nations': the decree's opening words and its name.

carryVoice: Pocket this one: sent by nature, never by force, and never as a pitch. See you soon.
